osool-210.title: Chicken in Tomato Sauce (Dama)
osool-210.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

osool-210-i5.name: For the sauce: stock or water

instructions.1: Prepare and cut up the chicken, brown it in the ghee and lift it out.
instructions.2: For the sauce: fry the chopped onion in the remaining ghee, then add the strained tomatoes and cook until done; add the stock, season and bring to a boil.
instructions.3: Put the chicken pieces in the sauce, cover the pot and cook over low heat until tender, adding some water if needed.
instructions.4: Second method: cut a half-boiled chicken into 4 to 8 pieces and brown them in ghee; make the sauce with the remaining ghee and the chicken cooking broth, then continue as above.

osool-211.title: Pigeon and Vegetable Tagine
osool-211.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

instructions.1: Clean the pigeons, split them in half and season with salt and pepper, then sauté in the ghee and lift out.
instructions.2: Arrange the vegetables in the tagine in alternating layers with the sautéed pigeons in the middle.
instructions.3: Add the strained tomatoes, the ghee left from browning, a little water, salt and pepper.
instructions.4: Cover the tagine and bake in a hot oven for half an hour, then lower the heat and cook until done.
instructions.5: Second method: sauté the pigeons and lift them out, then sauté the vegetables in the remaining ghee; layer the vegetables and pigeons in the tagine, cover with the tomatoes and water, season, and bake covered until done.

osool-212.title: Braised Chicken with New Potatoes
osool-212.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

instructions.1: Prepare the chicken and season the inside with salt and pepper; put the liver, gizzard and two cardamom pods inside, then brown it whole in the ghee.
instructions.2: Add the onion, celery, carrot and a liter of water and cook over medium heat until tender.
instructions.3: Lift out the chicken, cut it into 4 pieces and remove the breastbone; keep it in a warm place, then strain the remaining sauce to remove the bits of vegetable.
instructions.4: Peel the small potatoes and fry them in a little ghee, then add the strained sauce and cook for about 10 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
instructions.5: Arrange the chicken pieces on a warm plate with the potatoes around them, then pour the sauce over.

osool-213.title: Braised Pigeons in Espagnole Sauce
osool-213.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

osool-213-i2.name: Espagnole sauce (brown sauce with tomato and vegetables)

instructions.1: Prepare the pigeons and cut each into four pieces.
instructions.2: Heat the ghee until very hot, brown the pieces and lift them out; then brown the boiled onions, lift them out and season.
instructions.3: Bring the espagnole sauce to a boil, add the pigeons and season; cover the pot and cook over low heat until the pigeons are tender.
instructions.4: Arrange the fried bread pieces on a warm plate, place the pigeon pieces on them and strain the sauce over.
instructions.5: Garnish the plate with the peas, carrots and onions.

osool-214.title: Chicken Külbastı (Pressed Pan-Fried Spring Chickens)
osool-214.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

osool-214-i7.name: Fried potatoes and parsley, for garnish

instructions.1: Clean the chickens and prepare them by splitting them along the back; remove the breastbone and ribs and flatten them with a cleaver.
instructions.2: Season with salt, pepper, onion juice and lemon juice for at least a quarter of an hour.
instructions.3: Heat the ghee in a pan until very hot and lay the chickens in it; cover with a flat lid and weigh it down, and cook until the underside browns, then turn over and brown the other side.
instructions.4: Add the water and 1 tablespoon lemon juice, lower the heat and cook until done.
instructions.5: Lift out and place on a warm plate as they are, or cut each in two; garnish with the potatoes and parsley and drizzle with the remaining juices.
instructions.6: Pigeon külbastı: made the same way; the pigeons may also be left whole, trussed and cooked in a small pot instead of a pan.

osool-215.title: Pot-Roasted Turkey (Külbastı)
osool-215.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

osool-215-i4.name: Two onions, a piece of celery and a piece of carrot

instructions.1: Prepare and truss the turkey and season with salt and pepper.
instructions.2: Heat the ghee until very hot, add the mastic and cardamom, then brown the turkey.
instructions.3: Add the chopped vegetables and a little water, cover the pot and leave over fairly low heat.
instructions.4: Lift the lid from time to time, turn the turkey and add some water, and continue until it is fully cooked.
instructions.5: Lift it out of the pot and serve hot with the fluffy rice; strain the remaining liquid in the pot and serve it hot in a sauceboat.

osool-216.title: Pigeons Stuffed with Bread and Liver
osool-216.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

osool-216-i6.name: The pigeons' livers, cooked and chopped

instructions.1: Pluck the pigeons dry, open them along the back and remove the breastbone.
instructions.2: Mix the onion, garlic, bread, parsley and livers, knead everything well with the egg and season with salt, pepper and allspice; stuff the pigeons with it and sew them closed.
instructions.3: Heat the ghee until very hot and brown the pigeons in it, then add a little water, lower the heat and cook until done.
instructions.4: Lift out of the pot, place on a plate, garnish with parsley and fried potatoes and pour the remaining liquid over them.
instructions.5: Chicken with bread stuffing: made the same way using a pair of spring chickens instead of pigeons.

osool-217.title: Boned Pigeons Stuffed with Minced Meat
osool-217.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

osool-217-i6.name: Ghee
osool-217-i6.standardAmount: 1 tablespoon (for the stuffing) and 1 tablespoon for browning

osool-217-i8.name: An onion, a piece of celery and the pigeon bones

osool-217-i10.name: Glaze or green relish (kamikh), for garnish

instructions.1: Pluck the pigeons dry, open them along the back, remove the bones and clean them well.
instructions.2: Mix the stuffing ingredients and season well; stuff the pigeons with it and sew them closed, then wrap each in paper greased with ghee on both sides and tie the paper securely.
instructions.3: Heat the ghee until very hot and brown the pigeons in it, then add a little water along with the bones, the onion, the celery and salt; cover the pot and leave over low heat.
instructions.4: Lift the lid from time to time, turn the pigeons and baste them with a little water, until they are cooked.
instructions.5: Lift out of the pot, remove the paper, wrap them in fresh paper and leave until completely cold.
instructions.6: Leave them whole, perhaps brushed with glaze and garnished with green relish, or cut into slices and garnish.

osool-218.title: Pigeon and Freekeh Tagine
osool-218.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

osool-218-i3.name: Chicken stock or the pigeon cooking broth

instructions.1: Prepare the freekeh and brown it lightly in the ghee, then add the liquid, salt and pepper and boil for 5 to 10 minutes with the pot covered.
instructions.2: Put half the freekeh in the tagine, then the pigeon, then the remaining freekeh.
instructions.3: Cover the tagine and bake in a fairly low oven until done.
instructions.4: Heat 1 teaspoon of ghee until very hot and sprinkle it over the top, then remove the lid for 5 minutes so the top browns.
instructions.5: Wrap a paper frill around the tagine and serve on a plate that suits its size.
instructions.6: Pigeon tagine with rice: made the same way using 1 small cup of rice instead of freekeh, with half the liquid milk and the other half pigeon broth.
instructions.7: Quail tagine with rice: 6 half-boiled quail, 1 small cup rice, 2 small cups quail broth and 1 tablespoon ghee, cooked like the pigeon tagine with rice.

osool-219.title: Fried Chicken with Sautéed Peas
osool-219.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)
osool-219.culturalNotes: Young birds are best for frying.

instructions.1: Drain the boiled chickens and pat them dry; fry them whole or in pieces, lift out of the ghee and sprinkle with a little salt and pepper.
instructions.2: Arrange on a warm plate, garnish with the fried potatoes and sautéed vegetables, and serve with the tomato sauce in a sauceboat.
instructions.3: Fried pigeons: lift a pair of boiled pigeons out of the cooking water, pat dry and fry in very hot ghee; drain on paper and serve with fried potatoes and sautéed vegetables, or with triangles of white bread fried in ghee.

osool-220.title: Oven-Browned Turkey
osool-220.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

osool-220-i4.name: For garnish: fluffy rice, fried vermicelli, artichokes stuffed with vegetables, stuffed tomatoes, or fried potatoes and brown sauce

instructions.1: Half-boil the turkey, then lift it out, pat dry and place it in a tray greased with ghee.
instructions.2: Cover the top with a little ghee and put the tray in the oven until it is cooked and browned on top, basting it from time to time with the ghee in the tray.
instructions.3: Place it on a large oblong plate and garnish with any of the listed accompaniments.
instructions.4: Quicker method: dry the boiled turkey thoroughly, then fry it in ghee on the stove; sprinkle the top with salt and pepper and serve garnished.

osool-221.title: Browned Duck or Goose with Roqaq
osool-221.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

osool-221-i4.name: Roqaq (thin baked pastry sheets) and parsley, for serving

instructions.1: Brown the boiled duck in very hot ghee, then lift it out and sprinkle the top with salt and pepper.
instructions.2: Place it on an oblong plate, garnish with parsley and serve with the roqaq.

osool-222.title: Breaded Chicken with Mustard
osool-222.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

osool-222-i7.name: Fried potatoes and parsley, for garnish

instructions.1: Lift the chicken out of the cooking water before it is fully cooked, drain and pat dry.
instructions.2: Cut it into suitable pieces and remove the bones and skin.
instructions.3: Coat the pieces in the flour mixed with the mustard, salt and pepper.
instructions.4: Coat in egg and breadcrumbs and shallow- or deep-fry in ghee, then lift onto paper to absorb the ghee.
instructions.5: Arrange on a warm plate and garnish with the potatoes and parsley.

osool-223.title: Pigeon Cutlets with Sausage
osool-223.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

instructions.1: Clean the pigeons, cut each in half and remove the bones except the thigh bone.
instructions.2: Season the pieces well with salt and pepper and shape them as much as possible like cutlets.
instructions.3: Heat the ghee until very hot and brown the pigeon pieces on both sides, then lift them out, cover with paper and weigh them down to keep their shape; leave like this until cold.
instructions.4: Cover both sides of the pieces with sausage meat and smooth it well.
instructions.5: Coat in egg and breadcrumbs and fry in very hot ghee.
instructions.6: Arrange the pieces on a ring of mashed potatoes with the sautéed vegetables in the middle and serve with tomato sauce.

osool-224.title: Chicken in Batter
osool-224.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

instructions.1: Cut the chicken into fairly small, even pieces and remove the bones and skin.
instructions.2: Mix the marinade ingredients, add the chicken pieces and turn them from time to time; leave for half an hour, then lift out, pat dry and coat in a little flour.
instructions.3: Dip them in the batter, lift out carefully and deep-fry in plenty of ghee.
instructions.4: Lift out of the ghee and drain on paper, then place on a plate lined with a paper doily, garnish with parsley and serve with tomato sauce.

osool-225.title: Grilled Pigeons
osool-225.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)
osool-225.culturalNotes: Birds for grilling must be young; pigeons and very small chickens are used most often.

osool-225-i5.name: Sautéed peas, grilled tomatoes, lemon and parsley, for serving

instructions.1: Prepare the pigeons and split them along the back; remove the breastbone and ribs or leave them in.
instructions.2: Season with lemon juice, onion juice, salt and pepper and leave for half an hour.
instructions.3: Grill over charcoal like meat, leaving each bird whole or splitting it in two.
instructions.4: Arrange on the plate and garnish with the sautéed peas, grilled tomatoes, lemon and parsley.
instructions.5: Grilled spring chickens: clean 2 spring chickens, split them along the back, remove the breastbone and ribs and flatten with a cleaver; season with salt, pepper, lemon juice and onion juice for a quarter of an hour, brush with warm ghee and grill over charcoal; split each in two and garnish with parsley, lemon and fried potatoes.

osool-226.title: Roast Duck with Onion Stuffing and Apple Sauce
osool-226.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

osool-226-i2.name: For the onion stuffing: chopped onions

osool-226-i3.name: For the onion stuffing: stale white breadcrumbs

osool-226-i6.name: For the onion stuffing: egg or milk for binding

instructions.1: For the onion stuffing: rub the onions with salt, pepper and allspice, add the thyme, ghee and breadcrumbs and mix everything well; bind with egg or milk into a fairly soft mixture.
instructions.2: Clean and prepare the duck like a chicken, then fill it with the onion stuffing.
instructions.3: Place in a tray greased with ghee and put the ghee on top of it.
instructions.4: Roast in a fairly hot oven until done (one to one and a half hours), basting with ghee from time to time.
instructions.5: Place on a plate, garnish with parsley, pour the brown sauce around it and serve with the apple sauce.
instructions.6: Roast goose: made with the same ingredients and method.

osool-227.title: Duck Stuffed with Liver and Breadcrumbs
osool-227.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

osool-227-i7.name: Melted ghee
osool-227-i7.standardAmount: 1 tablespoon (for the stuffing) and 1 tablespoon for the tray

instructions.1: Clean the duck, wash it well and season the inside with salt and pepper.
instructions.2: Chop the liver and add the seasoning, onion, breadcrumbs, parsley and melted ghee; mix everything well and bind with egg.
instructions.3: Fill the duck with the mixture and truss it, then place it in a tray and cover with the ghee.
instructions.4: Roast in a hot oven for a quarter of an hour, basting from time to time with the ghee in the tray.
instructions.5: Pour the ghee out of the tray and replace it with the brown sauce; return the duck to the oven to finish cooking at a somewhat lower heat, basting it from time to time with the brown sauce.
instructions.6: Lift out of the tray and place on a hot plate with the sauce around it.

osool-228.title: Roast Chicken with New Potatoes
osool-228.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

instructions.1: Prepare the chicken, season with salt and pepper and truss it; place it in a tray greased with ghee, cover with greased paper and put the ghee on top.
instructions.2: Roast in a hot oven for a quarter of an hour, then lower the heat and cook until done, opening the oven every quarter of an hour to baste it with the ghee in the tray.
instructions.3: Add the peeled small potatoes half an hour before it is done.
instructions.4: Remove the paper, place the chicken on a plate, garnish with the potatoes or parsley and serve with the brown sauce.

osool-301.title: Rabbit in White Sauce or Parsley Sauce
osool-301.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

osool-301-i3.name: Mastic and cardamom
osool-301-i3.standardAmount: 2 small pieces of mastic and 2 cardamom pods

osool-301-i5.name: White sauce (half milk, half rabbit broth)

osool-301-i6.name: Parsley sauce (white sauce with chopped parsley)

osool-301-i7.name: Boiled diced carrots and boiled peas, for garnish

instructions.1: Put the cut rabbit in a pot without any liquid and heat gently with the lid on for 3 to 5 minutes, then lift the lid and discard the liquid released; repeat once more.
instructions.2: Add the tablespoon of ghee and sauté the pieces, then add the mastic, cardamom, enough water to cover, the onion and salt, and cook until tender.
instructions.3: Make the white sauce from the rabbit broth and milk, and make the parsley sauce.
instructions.4: Arrange the rabbit pieces neatly on a warm plate, cover with the sauce and garnish with the carrots and peas.

osool-302.title: Braised Rabbit with Vegetables in Lemon White Sauce
osool-302.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

instructions.1: Clean the rabbit and cut it into pieces; prepare the vegetables and cut them into cubes.
instructions.2: Heat the ghee until very hot, sauté the pieces and lift them out, then stir the flour in the remaining ghee without letting it brown.
instructions.3: Take the pot off the heat and add the water, stirring constantly.
instructions.4: Season the sauce with salt and white pepper, add the sautéed rabbit and the vegetables, cover the pot and cook over low heat until everything is tender.
instructions.5: Add the lemon juice and season; ladle into a deep dish and serve hot.

osool-303.title: Rabbit and Vegetable Tagine
osool-303.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

instructions.1: Clean and cut up the rabbit and prepare the vegetables.
instructions.2: Sauté the rabbit and lift it out, then brown the onion in the remaining ghee, add the flour and stir with the onion until it browns.
instructions.3: Take the pot off the heat and add the water gradually, stirring constantly, to make a brown sauce; season it.
instructions.4: Put half the vegetables in the tagine, then the sautéed rabbit, then the rest of the vegetables, and pour the brown sauce over.
instructions.5: Cover the tagine and bake in a moderate oven until done.
instructions.6: Wrap a paper frill around the tagine, fix it with a pin and serve hot.
instructions.7: Rabbit in browned flour sauce, tomato sauce or curry: cook it the same way as chicken in browned flour sauce, in tomato sauce or in curry.

osool-304.title: Fried Rabbit
osool-304.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

osool-304-i4.name: Fried potatoes and parsley, for garnish

instructions.1: Lift the pieces out of the cooking water, pat dry and fry in very hot ghee.
instructions.2: Sprinkle with salt and pepper, garnish with parsley and the fried potatoes and serve hot.

osool-305.title: Breaded Rabbit Pieces with Mayonnaise
osool-305.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

instructions.1: Cut the rabbit into pieces as even as possible.
instructions.2: Heat the ghee until very hot, lower the heat and sauté the pieces until browned and nearly cooked.
instructions.3: Break the eggs, beat them and season with salt and pepper; add the warm ghee left from sautéing, then coat the pieces in flour.
instructions.4: Brush the pieces with the egg and ghee mixture, then coat in breadcrumbs and fry in ghee.
instructions.5: Serve on a warm plate garnished with parsley, with the mayonnaise with pickles in a sauceboat.

osool-951.title: Chicken in Aspic Mold
osool-951.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)
osool-951.culturalNotes: Savory aspic (gelatina) is seasoned stock clarified with egg white, with gelatin added so it sets clear; it is used for serving cold meats, poultry and fish. Use on average 40 to 60 g gelatin per liter of liquid, depending on the weather.

osool-951-i1.name: Medium chicken, boiled and cut into even pieces

osool-951-i3.name: For the aspic: vinegar and lemon juice

osool-951-i4.name: For the aspic: halal (beef) gelatin sheets

osool-951-i5.name: For the aspic: salt and black peppercorns

osool-951-i6.name: For the aspic: thinly pared zest of two lemons, an onion, a piece of celery, a piece of carrot and 3 cloves

osool-951-i7.name: For clarifying: whites and shells of 3 eggs

instructions.1: For the clear aspic: soak the gelatin in a little water, then put it in a clean pot with the stock, vinegar, lemon, salt, spices, vegetables and the egg whites and washed, crushed shells; whisk over low heat until nearly boiling, then leave undisturbed until the set layer of egg white floats up; keep over very low heat for 10 minutes, then strain through a cloth until clear, and let it cool without setting.
instructions.2: Take a plain oblong mold, wet it with cold water, pour in a layer of aspic and leave it to set.
instructions.3: Arrange a neat layer of peas, gherkins and carrots on top, after dipping them in a little liquid aspic, followed by a layer of aspic.
instructions.4: Dip the chicken pieces in aspic and add them, then the vegetables, and so on until the mold is full, finishing with a layer of aspic.
instructions.5: Leave the mold until set, then turn it out onto an oblong plate lined with lettuce.
instructions.6: Meat in aspic: made like the chicken using cooked veal cut into cubes, with the meat cooking broth used to make the aspic.
instructions.7: Shrimp in aspic mold: ¼–½ kg boiled peeled shrimp, 2 boiled eggs and 2 pickled gherkins sliced into rounds; made the same way in a wet oblong mold and turned out onto a plate lined with lettuce.
instructions.8: Poultry in aspic: cut up boiled birds (a pair of pigeons, a chicken, two pairs of quail, or leftover turkey or duck) with ⅛ kg carrots and pickled gherkins and ¼ kg peas, keeping back a boiled egg and a few vegetables for garnish; mix with half the aspic and put in the dish until set, then pour a layer of aspic over the top and garnish with the egg and vegetables.

osool-952.title: Chaud-Froid Chicken Breasts with Mayonnaise
osool-952.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

osool-952-i1.name: Breasts of two cold boiled chickens

osool-952-i2.name: Savory aspic
osool-952-i2.standardAmount: ½ cup (and another ½ cup for serving)

instructions.1: Remove the skin and bone from the breasts and cut the meat neatly into suitable pieces, as even as possible.
instructions.2: Melt the aspic and let it cool without setting, then add it to the mayonnaise and stir well.
instructions.3: Arrange the chicken pieces on a wire rack or sieve with a plate underneath.
instructions.4: Spoon the sauce over the chicken pieces to coat them and leave until almost set.
instructions.5: Decorate the tops simply with thinly cut carrot and peas and leave until completely set.
instructions.6: Pour a little aspic over the decorated tops and leave until this layer sets.
instructions.7: Arrange the pieces on the Russian salad on a glass plate, surrounded by coarsely chopped aspic.
instructions.8: Chilled lamb chops in tomato sauce: season ½ kg lamb chops with salt and cook over low heat until they absorb their juices, then add water gradually until tender; lay them flat under a weight until cold, then coat with 1 cup tomato sauce set with gelatin, decorate with carrots, peas and pickled gherkins, cover with a layer of aspic and serve on a summer salad.

osool-953.title: Pigeon Tartlets in Aspic
osool-953.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

instructions.1: Cut the pigeon meat into cubes and mix with the chopped gherkins and half the aspic.
instructions.2: Pile the meat into the pastry cases in a mound and leave until set.
instructions.3: Cover the meat with a layer of clear aspic and leave until set.
instructions.4: Place a fine sprig of parsley in the center of each tartlet.
instructions.5: Arrange the tartlets on a plate with the shredded lettuce in the middle.

osool-954.title: Eggs in Aspic
osool-954.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

osool-954-i5.name: Lettuce salad dressed with a little French dressing

instructions.1: Wet 6 to 8 small plain molds with water, then coat the bottoms and sides with a thin layer of aspic and leave to set on ice.
instructions.2: Cut the carrots into decorative shapes; dip the carrot pieces and peas in a little cold liquid aspic and fix them on the bottom over the set layer to form a pattern; leave to set, then pour a little aspic over and leave to set.
instructions.3: Cut the boiled eggs into rounds or lengthwise quarters and arrange over the aspic layer; fill the mold with aspic and leave to set.
instructions.4: Turn the molds out onto the bed of dressed lettuce.
instructions.5: Eggs in aspic (no. 2): wet 6 dariole molds and pour in aspic ½ cm deep; leave to set, then cut pickled gherkin and fix it on top in a pattern, followed by a layer of aspic; trim a thin slice from the wide end of each egg, dip in aspic and stand it in the mold, and fill the space around it with aspic until set; turn out onto a plate and scatter shredded lettuce around.

osool-955.title: Steamed Cheese Timbales on Spinach (Vegetarian)
osool-955.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)
osool-955.culturalNotes: One of the book's vegetarian dishes, in which eggs and cheese take the place of meat.

osool-955-i6.name: Light white sauce or tomato sauce

instructions.1: Beat the eggs well and add the milk; stir the mixture, pour it over the breadcrumbs and leave for 10 minutes, then add the cheese and season.
instructions.2: Pour the mixture into small molds well greased with ghee and cover the molds with paper greased with ghee.
instructions.3: Steam the molds for half an hour.
instructions.4: Turn out onto a bed of spinach purée and serve with the chosen sauce in a sauceboat.

osool-956.title: Vegetarian Hazelnut Cutlets
osool-956.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

osool-956-i11.name: Potato purée and tomato sauce, for serving

instructions.1: Brown the onion and hazelnuts in some of the ghee, then pass the onion, hazelnuts and bread through the mincer twice.
instructions.2: Mix everything well with the tomato juice and season the mixture.
instructions.3: Spread on a greased plate and smooth the top completely, then cut into equal pieces and shape like cutlets, inserting a piece of macaroni into the end of each.
instructions.4: Coat in egg and breadcrumbs and fry in the oil.
instructions.5: Arrange the cutlets on a bed of potato purée and pour the sauce around the bed.

osool-957.title: Vegetarian Baked Hazelnut Loaf
osool-957.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

osool-957-i11.name: Brown sauce made with vegetable stock, fried potatoes and sautéed vegetables, for serving

instructions.1: Fry the onion in the ghee, add the breadcrumbs and pass through the mincer.
instructions.2: Peel and chop the tomatoes, then combine all the ingredients and bind with the egg and the stock or water.
instructions.3: Pour the mixture into a greased mold coated with a layer of breadcrumbs.
instructions.4: Bake in a moderate oven for an hour and serve with a brown sauce made from vegetable stock, fried potatoes and sautéed vegetables.

osool-958.title: Baked Potatoes Filled with Egg and Cheese
osool-958.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

instructions.1: Wash the potatoes well, dry them and bake in their skins in the oven.
instructions.2: Hollow out the potatoes to remove some of the flesh and season the hollow with a little salt and pepper.
instructions.3: Put the cream in the hollow, then the egg; season with salt and pepper and sprinkle the top with the rumi cheese.
instructions.4: Return the potatoes to the oven until the eggs are cooked; serve on a plate lined with a folded napkin, garnished with parsley, with tomato sauce if you like.

osool-959.title: Potato Croquettes Filled with Chestnuts
osool-959.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

instructions.1: Mix the chestnuts, lemon zest, white sauce and seasoning and knead well.
instructions.2: Mash the boiled potatoes, knead with the butter and egg yolk and season well.
instructions.3: Form the potato into balls of equal size, make a hollow in the center of each, fill with some of the chestnut filling and seal each ball completely.
instructions.4: Coat the balls in egg and breadcrumbs and deep-fry in plenty of ghee.
instructions.5: Garnish with parsley and serve with tomato sauce.

osool-960.title: Vegetarian Scotch Eggs with Lentils
osool-960.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

instructions.1: Cook the lentils with a little water and the piece of onion, then drain and mix with the remaining ingredients (parsley, lemon zest, butter, breadcrumbs and thyme); season well.
instructions.2: Peel the eggs and dust with a little flour, then cover with a layer of the lentil mixture, smoothing it well.
instructions.3: Coat in egg and breadcrumbs and deep-fry in plenty of ghee.
instructions.4: Cut each egg in half crosswise and serve hot or cold, like Scotch eggs.

osool-961.title: Steamed Chicken Mousse with Cream (for Invalids and Convalescents)
osool-961.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)
osool-961.culturalNotes: From the book's section on food for invalids and convalescents: an easily digested, lightly seasoned dish.

instructions.1: Pass the chicken twice through the fine plate of the mincer, then press through a wire sieve.
instructions.2: Add the eggs and the thick sauce, then the lightly whipped cream; season with salt, pepper and a little lemon juice.
instructions.3: Pour the mixture into a mold greased with ghee and cover with greased paper.
instructions.4: Steam for half an hour.
instructions.5: Turn out and pour the béchamel sauce around it.
instructions.6: Chicken mousse (no. 1): like the steamed fish mousse, using raw chicken instead of fish.
instructions.7: Chicken mousse (no. 3): like mousse no. 2, leaving out the cream and the béchamel sauce.

osool-962.title: Spring Chicken Broth and Chicken Tea (for the Sick)
osool-962.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

osool-962-i1.name: Prepared spring chicken (a very small chicken)

instructions.1: Cut the chicken meat into small pieces.
instructions.2: Put it in a liter of cold water with a pinch of salt and cook over low heat until the meat falls apart completely.
instructions.3: Strain the broth and serve.
instructions.4: Chicken tea: cut the chicken meat into very thin pieces and soak in a full cup of water for a few minutes; add the salt and ¼ kg milk and put in a covered jar standing in a pot of water over low heat for 3 hours; strain, remove the fat and serve hot with toasted bread.

osool-963.title: Baked Fish Custard (for the Sick)
osool-963.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)

osool-963-i4.name: A little salt and white pepper

instructions.1: Steam the fish as for steamed fish (between two greased plates over boiling water).
instructions.2: Beat the egg lightly, add the milk and season with salt and pepper; stir and strain the mixture (custard).
instructions.3: Place the fish in a greased ovenproof dish, pour the custard over it and stand the dish in a tray of water.
instructions.4: Bake in a low oven until the custard sets.
instructions.5: Serve hot, garnished with parsley and lemon.

osool-964.title: Onion Stuffing for Poultry (and Bread Stuffing)
osool-964.chapter: From Osool El Tahy (Principles of Cooking)
osool-964.culturalNotes: A stuffing the book uses with many oven-baked stuffed poultry, meat and fish dishes.

instructions.1: Rub the onions with salt, pepper and allspice.
instructions.2: Add the thyme, ghee and breadcrumbs and mix everything well.
instructions.3: Bind with egg or milk into a fairly soft mixture and use it to stuff duck, goose or meat before cooking in the oven.
instructions.4: Bread stuffing: 1 full cup stale white breadcrumbs, 1 tablespoon chopped parsley, the grated zest and juice of a lemon, 1 tablespoon ghee, ¼ teaspoon allspice, ¼ teaspoon salt and a little white pepper; mix and bind with egg or milk into a soft mixture, and use to stuff poultry, fish and meat.

ec-003.title: Cold Black-Eyed Bean Salad (Lubya Nashfa Barda)
ec-003.culturalNotes: Recipe 3, page 6 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Leave the beans to soak in plenty of water overnight.
instructions.2: Drain them, cover with fresh water and boil for about 30 minutes, until tender.
instructions.3: Drain again and spread the beans out on a tray so they cool quickly without turning mushy.
instructions.4: Pound the garlic with a little salt, then stir in the lemon juice, oil and pepper.
instructions.5: Pour the garlic dressing over the cool beans and fold it through gently so every bean is coated.
instructions.6: Onion and mint version (recipe 339 in the book): boil one onion with the beans, adding the salt for the last 5 minutes. Once cool, toss the beans with a second, finely chopped onion, a few fresh mint leaves and a simple dressing of oil, lemon juice, a little vinegar, salt and pepper.

ec-005.title: Fried Kubeiba Discs (Kubeiba A'ras)
ec-005.culturalNotes: Recipe 5, page 7 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Soak the bulgur in cold water until it swells, then drain and squeeze it dry in a cloth.
instructions.2: Mince the beef finely, then mix the minced meat with the squeezed bulgur, grated onion, salt and pepper.
instructions.3: Knead the mixture with hands in a bowl full of icy water, folding it over and over until it is very light and feels like a mousse.
instructions.4: Form the mixture into patties with well-oiled hands, pressing them flat and even.
instructions.5: Fry the discs in deep hot fat until brown on both sides.
instructions.6: Drain on absorbent paper and serve hot.

ec-007.title: Houmous (Hummus)
ec-007.culturalNotes: Recipe 7, page 8 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Blend or pound the hot chickpeas to a paste.
instructions.2: Pound the garlic with salt, then add the tahini and blend into the chickpeas.
instructions.3: Add the lemon juice slowly, beating hard to incorporate it.
instructions.4: Spread the hummus on a shallow dish.
instructions.5: Option: pour a little hot olive oil over it and sprinkle with paprika and parsley.

ec-008.title: Mashed Broad Beans, Warm and Cold (Foul Medames)
ec-008.culturalNotes: Recipe 8, page 8 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-008-i1.name: Dried Broad Beans Or Split Fava Beans (foul)

instructions.1: Soak the beans overnight in plenty of water.
instructions.2: Drain the beans, cover with fresh water and simmer very gently for 3–4 hours, until the beans fall apart easily.
instructions.3: Fry the sliced garlic in the oil until pale gold, add salt and pepper and pour over the beans.
instructions.4: Squeeze the lemon juice over the top and stir.
instructions.5: Serve warm with hard-boiled egg halves on top.

ec-010.title: Spinach and Walnut Dip (Mahammara)
ec-010.culturalNotes: Recipe 10, page 9 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Blanch the spinach briefly in boiling water, then drain and squeeze it very dry.
instructions.2: Mix the chopped spinach with the ground walnuts and crushed garlic.
instructions.3: Add the pomegranate molasses or tamarind water, oil, salt and pepper.
instructions.4: Mix well and serve at room temperature.

ec-012.title: Cheese and Yogurt Dip (Labneh Maakhal)
ec-012.culturalNotes: Recipe 12, page 10 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Mix the labneh with the crushed garlic, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
instructions.2: Spoon into a shallow dish and make a well in the centre.
instructions.3: Pour a little olive oil into the well.

ec-014.title: Tabbouleh (Parsley Salad)
ec-014.culturalNotes: Recipe 14, page 11 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Soak the bulgur in cold water until it swells, then drain well.
instructions.2: Finely chop the parsley leaves (not the stems) and the mint.
instructions.3: Peel and finely chop the tomatoes.
instructions.4: Mix the bulgur, parsley, mint, tomatoes and onion in a bowl.
instructions.5: Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper together, then pour over the salad.
instructions.6: Toss and serve at room temperature.

ec-042.title: Eggs Fried with Garlic and Mint (Beid Ma'li ma' Toom)
ec-042.culturalNotes: Recipe 42, page 23 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Crush the garlic with a little salt and stir in the lemon juice.
instructions.2: Fry the garlic mixture briefly in the oil.
instructions.3: Slide the eggs into the pan and fry them, spooning the hot garlicky oil over them once or twice.
instructions.4: Sprinkle with the mint, salt and pepper and serve.

ec-043.title: Eggs Fried with Lemon Juice (Beid Ma'li ma' Lamun)
ec-043.culturalNotes: Recipe 43, page 23 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Heat the oil until it sizzles and slide in the eggs.
instructions.2: Pour the lemon juice over them straight away.
instructions.3: Baste the eggs with the pan juices once or twice as they set.
instructions.4: Season with salt and pepper and serve.

ec-048.title: Egg and Yogurt Sandwich Spread (Beid bi-l-Zabadi)
ec-048.culturalNotes: Recipe 48, page 25 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Peel the eggs and mash them with a fork.
instructions.2: Mix in the yogurt, mustard, salt and pepper.
instructions.3: Spread on bread for sandwiches.

ec-052.title: Herb and Sumac Omelet ('Igga bi-l-Tawabil)
ec-052.culturalNotes: Recipe 52, page 26 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Beat the eggs with the sifted flour, herbs, spices, salt and pepper.
instructions.2: Fry the finely chopped onion in the oil until pale gold, then pour in the eggs over a high heat.
instructions.3: As the bottom sets, tilt the pan or lift the edge so the runny egg flows underneath.
instructions.4: Turn the omelet and fry until both sides are golden and dry.

ec-059.title: Dukkah Spice and Nut Dip (Du''a)
ec-059.culturalNotes: Recipe 59, page 27 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Grind all the ingredients together in a mortar or a blender.
instructions.2: Eat by dipping pieces of baladi bread into the mixture.

ec-060.title: Homemade Labneh (Labna)
ec-060.culturalNotes: Recipe 60, page 27 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Stir the salt into the yogurt.
instructions.2: Pour it into a wet cheesecloth bag, tie the top and hang it for 24 hours over a clean bowl.
instructions.3: Keep the whey that drips out; it is nourishing and can be drunk or used in cooking.
instructions.4: Spoon the labneh into a jar and pour a little oil, preferably olive oil, over the top.
instructions.5: Labneh balls for keeping: hang a larger batch for longer, opening the bag every 24 hours to stir the yogurt (it thickens faster near the cloth) and adding a little more salt each day. When it is thick and even all through, roll small amounts into balls with wet hands and keep them in a jar half full of olive oil.

ec-061.title: Homemade Pastirma (Bastirma)
ec-061.culturalNotes: Recipe 61, page 28 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-061-i1.name: Beef Fillet Or Another Prime Cut

instructions.1: Trim every bit of fat from the meat, dry it well and make two or three very shallow cuts in the surface.
instructions.2: Roll the meat in 1/4 cup of the salt so it is completely covered.
instructions.3: Lay it on a rack with a weight on top so the juices drain away, and leave it for 3–4 days.
instructions.4: Take off the weight, wipe the meat dry and thread a cord through one end, leaving a long loop for hanging.
instructions.5: Peel and crush the garlic and knead it with the fenugreek, chili and the rest of the salt into a soft paste.
instructions.6: Coat the meat with the paste in a layer 1/2–1 cm thick.
instructions.7: Hang it for another 3–4 days, until it is thoroughly dry and dark brown.
instructions.8: Slice paper-thin and eat it raw at breakfast, with or without the rind, or fry it with eggs or use it in pastries.

ec-062.title: Sweet Vermicelli with Raisins (Sha'riya)
ec-062.culturalNotes: Recipe 62, page 28 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Break the vermicelli with your fingers into pieces 2–3 cm long.
instructions.2: Fry the raisins lightly in the oil until they puff up, then lift them out.
instructions.3: Fry the vermicelli in the same oil until pale brown.
instructions.4: Dissolve the sugar in the boiling water and pour it over the vermicelli, add the raisins, and cook over a low heat for about 15 minutes.
instructions.5: If the water is absorbed before the vermicelli is tender, sprinkle in a little more hot water.
instructions.6: Serve with warm milk poured over each plate.
instructions.7: For a buffet dessert, add chopped bananas, strawberries and mixed nuts.

ec-064.title: Eggs with Fried White Cheese (Beid Ma'li ma' Jibneh Beida)
ec-064.culturalNotes: Recipe 64, page 29 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-064-i2.name: Hard White Cheese, In 1 Cm Slices

instructions.1: Fry the cheese one slice at a time, turning it to colour both sides, and keep it warm at the side of the serving dish.
instructions.2: Fry the eggs in the same oil, basting them as they cook.
instructions.3: Serve the eggs next to the fried cheese, sprinkled with salt and pepper.

ec-065.title: Yemeni Fatut with Fenugreek (Fatut bi-l-Hulba)
ec-065.culturalNotes: Recipe 65, page 29 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Blend the fenugreek, tomato paste and zhug into a paste.
instructions.2: Tear the bread into bite-sized pieces and fry them in the ghee until crisp.
instructions.3: Add the eggs to the pan and stir until they are well set and scrambled with the bread.
instructions.4: Boil the chicken stock with the fenugreek paste, uncovered and over a high heat, until reduced by half.
instructions.5: Add the egg and bread mixture and cook for 3–5 minutes more, then season.
instructions.6: Serve with a little lemon juice added to each plate.

ec-066.title: Turkish Eggs on Spinach and Feta (Ispanaklı Yumurta)
ec-066.culturalNotes: Recipe 66, page 30 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Wash the spinach in several changes of water, drain it in a colander and shred it coarsely.
instructions.2: Fry the onion in the oil until it softens.
instructions.3: Add the spinach and stir over a medium heat until the leaves wilt and release their liquid.
instructions.4: Turn up the heat and cook until only enough liquid is left to cover the bottom of the pan.
instructions.5: Stir in the crumbled cheese, salt and pepper.
instructions.6: Break the eggs onto the spinach, spacing them evenly, cover the pan and cook over a medium heat until the eggs are set.

ec-067.title: Turkish Poached Eggs in Garlic Yogurt (Çılbır)
ec-067.culturalNotes: Recipe 67, page 30 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Mix the yogurt with the garlic, salt and pepper and warm it in an ovenproof dish in a moderately hot oven.
instructions.2: Meanwhile, poach the eggs in simmering water with the vinegar and, once set, lay them on the yogurt.
instructions.3: Melt the butter, stir in the paprika and drizzle the red butter over the eggs.
instructions.4: Return the dish to the oven for 2–3 minutes, then serve on individual plates and season to taste.

ec-068.title: Lebanese Baked Eggs in Yogurt (Beid bi-l-Laban)
ec-068.culturalNotes: Recipe 68, page 31 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Whisk the egg white until stiff and stir it into the yogurt; this keeps the yogurt from splitting.
instructions.2: Cook the yogurt uncovered over a very low heat for 5–7 minutes, then pour it into a shallow ovenproof dish.
instructions.3: Fry the garlic in the ghee until golden, stirring all the time so it does not stick, then stir in the mint, salt and pepper.
instructions.4: Break the eggs over the yogurt, spacing them evenly, and pour the garlic ghee over them.
instructions.5: Bake until the eggs are set.

ec-069.title: Tunisian Ojja with Merguez and Potatoes (Ojja bi Mergaz)
ec-069.culturalNotes: Recipe 69, page 31 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-069-i2.name: Potatoes, Peeled And Diced Very Small

ec-069-i3.name: Lamb or Beef Merguez Sausages, Chopped Small

instructions.1: Pound the garlic with salt, the paprika and the caraway.
instructions.2: Sauté the potatoes in the oil, then add the tomato paste, the garlic mixture, the harissa and just enough water to cover.
instructions.3: Cook over a low heat for 15 minutes.
instructions.4: Add the sausages and cook for another 15 minutes.
instructions.5: Beat the eggs with salt and pepper, pour them over the stew and stir.
instructions.6: Serve as soon as the eggs are set.

ec-070.title: Brain Omelet (Ijjit Nukha'aat)
ec-070.culturalNotes: Recipe 70, page 32 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Parboil the brain in salted water, drain it, remove the veins and mash it.
instructions.2: Soften the onion in ghee, add the garlic and fry until golden, stirring all the time, then take the pan off the heat.
instructions.3: Beat the eggs and stir in the brain, the onion and garlic, the lemon juice, parsley, salt and pepper.
instructions.4: Heat more ghee and pour in the egg mixture. As the bottom sets, lift the edge so the runny egg flows underneath.
instructions.5: Turn the omelet and fry until both sides are golden and set.
instructions.6: Cut into thick wedges and serve.

ec-071.title: Persian Eggplant Kuku (Kuku-ye Bademjan)
ec-071.culturalNotes: Recipe 71, page 32 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Peel and dice the eggplants, sprinkle them with salt and leave for an hour.
instructions.2: Squeeze them dry, fry until golden, then mash them in a deep bowl.
instructions.3: Beat in the eggs, onion, cumin, salt and pepper until smooth.
instructions.4: Heat ghee in a pan and pour in the mixture. As the bottom sets, lift the edge so the uncooked egg runs underneath.
instructions.5: Turn the kuku over and fry until both sides are brown.
instructions.6: Cut into thick wedges and serve with yogurt spooned over each plate.

ec-072.title: Persian Potato Kuku or Patties (Kuku-ye Sibzamini)
ec-072.culturalNotes: Recipe 72, page 33 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Peel and boil the potatoes, then mash them in a deep bowl.
instructions.2: Mix in the eggs, onion, turmeric, salt and pepper until smooth.
instructions.3: Heat ghee and fry the mixture like a thick omelet, lifting the edge as the bottom sets so the uncooked egg runs underneath.
instructions.4: Turn it over and fry until brown on both sides.
instructions.5: Cut into thick wedges and serve.
instructions.6: Patties: drop spoonfuls of the mixture into hot ghee, flatten them and deep-fry, then drain on absorbent paper.

ec-076.title: Artichokes and Peas in Garlic Butter (Kharshuf Matbukh)
ec-076.culturalNotes: Recipe 76, page 35 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Trim the artichokes down to their hearts and cut each heart into 4–6 pieces.
instructions.2: Parboil the peas, add the artichokes and boil together until both are tender, then drain.
instructions.3: Crush the garlic with salt and work it into the butter until smooth.
instructions.4: Warm the garlic butter over a very low heat until the garlic turns pale yellow.
instructions.5: Add the vegetables and simmer for about 10 minutes, tossing often.

ec-081.title: Tunisian Stuffed Artichoke Hearts (Gannariya Mihshiya)
ec-081.culturalNotes: Recipe 81, page 37 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Sauce: fry half the garlic in hot fat, stirring so it does not stick, then add the tomato paste, paprika, salt and pepper thinned with 2 cups of water and simmer for 5 minutes.
instructions.2: Filling: put the beef in a pot with half a cup of water over a high heat and stir until the water has evaporated. Add the onion and cook until soft, then add the parsley, the rest of the garlic, the tabil, salt and pepper and cook for 3 minutes more. Leave to cool.
instructions.3: Boil and mash the potato. Beat the eggs and mix them thoroughly into the meat with the potato.
instructions.4: Fill the artichoke hearts with the meat mixture and arrange them neatly in a pot.
instructions.5: Pour the tomato sauce over them and cook gently until the artichokes are tender.
instructions.6: Add the lemon juice before serving.

ec-085.title: Black-Eyed Beans and Beef in Tomato (Lubya Nashfa bi-l-Dim‘a)
ec-085.culturalNotes: Recipe 85, page 40 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-085-i6.name: Garlic Cloves, Peeled And Halved Diagonally

instructions.1: Soak the beans overnight, drain, then parboil them in fresh water for 5–7 minutes and drain again.
instructions.2: Cut the meat into small cubes and chop the onions.
instructions.3: Soften the onions in the oil, add the meat and fry until the juices it releases have been absorbed again.
instructions.4: Add the beans, parsley, chard, tomato juice, garlic, salt and pepper.
instructions.5: Cook over a low heat until the meat and beans are both tender.

ec-086.title: White Beans Stewed with Beef and Garlic (Fasulya Beida Matbukha)
ec-086.culturalNotes: Recipe 86, page 40 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-086-i4.name: Garlic Cloves, Peeled And Halved Diagonally

instructions.1: Soak the beans overnight, rinse them and boil for 15–30 minutes, until tender, skimming as needed. Drain and set aside.
instructions.2: Cut the meat into bite-sized pieces.
instructions.3: Fry the onions until golden brown, add the meat and fry until it has reabsorbed its juices.
instructions.4: Add the garlic, salt, pepper and just enough water to cover, and cook for about 20 minutes.
instructions.5: Add the beans and simmer for 10 minutes more.
instructions.6: In tomato sauce (recipe 87 in the book): fry the cubed meat until it reabsorbs its juices, simmer it in 2 cups of tomato sauce for 20 minutes, then add the boiled beans and simmer for 10 minutes.

ec-089.title: Turkish White Bean Stew (Fasulye Pilaki)
ec-089.culturalNotes: Recipe 89, page 41 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-089-i5.name: Celery Stalks And Leaves, Very Finely Sliced

instructions.1: Soak the beans for at least 2 hours. Drain, cover with plenty of fresh water, boil for 3–5 minutes, then take off the heat and leave for 1–2 hours.
instructions.2: Fry the onions in olive oil until soft, add the garlic, carrots and celery and fry for 3–5 minutes, stirring.
instructions.3: Bring the beans back to the boil and cook for 30 minutes.
instructions.4: Thin the tomato paste with water, add the sugar, salt and pepper, and add it to the beans with the fried vegetables. Cook until everything is tender.
instructions.5: Off the heat, stir in the lemon juice, parsley and chili if using, and check the seasoning. Serve hot or cold.

ec-098.title: Kibbeh in Yogurt with Chickpeas (Kubeiba Labaniya)
ec-098.culturalNotes: Recipe 98, page 45 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-098-i1.name: Kibbeh Paste (fine Bulgur, Beef, Fat And Onion)

instructions.1: Soak the chickpeas overnight, drain, and parboil in fresh water for 5–7 minutes. Drain.
instructions.2: Make kibbeh paste as for the fried kubeiba discs in this collection (bulgur soaked for an hour, then minced repeatedly with beef, fat and onion into a soft dough).
instructions.3: Either shape it into hollow balls filled with spiced minced beef and pine nuts, or cut it into thin discs. Do not fry them.
instructions.4: Put the kibbeh in a pot with the chickpeas.
instructions.5: Stir the egg white into the yogurt to stop it curdling and press it through a sieve over the kibbeh.
instructions.6: Cook uncovered for 60–90 minutes.
instructions.7: Sprinkle with the mint and serve hot or cold.

ec-105.title: Cauliflower Stewed with Beef and Tomato (‘Arnabit Matbukh)
ec-105.culturalNotes: Recipe 105, page 49 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Break the cauliflower into florets and cut the meat into bite-sized pieces. Peel and dice the tomatoes and chop the onions very finely.
instructions.2: Fry the onions in the oil until pale yellow, add the tomatoes and cook for 7–10 minutes.
instructions.3: Add the meat with salt and pepper and cook for about 20 minutes.
instructions.4: Add the cauliflower and simmer for about 10 minutes, until tender.
instructions.5: With garlic instead of tomato (recipe 106 in the book): fry the onions, brown the meat until it reabsorbs its juices, cover with water, add 7–10 halved garlic cloves with the seasoning and cook for 20 minutes, then add the cauliflower for 10 minutes.

ec-109.title: Baked Chicken with Tomatoes and Onions (Tagin Firakh)
ec-109.culturalNotes: Recipe 109, page 50 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut each chicken into 4–6 pieces.
instructions.2: Mix the spice with salt and pepper and rub it lightly over the chicken.
instructions.3: Lay the pieces in a lightly greased roasting pan and cover them with the seasoned onions and tomatoes.
instructions.4: Bake in a moderate, preheated oven for 60–90 minutes, basting with the pan juices.
instructions.5: Thicken the juices with cornflour if you like.
instructions.6: With carrots and celery (recipe 110 in the book): brown chopped onions and celery in oil, cover the chicken with them and with parboiled carrot rounds and halved garlic cloves, pour meat stock over and bake the same way.

ec-115.title: Chicken in Mastic Milk Sauce (Firakh Matbukha bi-l-Laban)
ec-115.culturalNotes: Recipe 115, page 53 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut each chicken into 6–8 pieces.
instructions.2: Heat the oil, stir in the mastic for 10 seconds, add the chicken, cover at once and turn off the heat. Leave for 1–2 minutes so the chicken takes on the scent.
instructions.3: Turn the heat back on and brown the chicken, then lift it out.
instructions.4: Fry the flour in the same oil until light brown. Off the heat, whisk in the milk a little at a time until smooth.
instructions.5: Return to the heat, season, and when it bubbles add the chicken.
instructions.6: Cook uncovered for about 20 minutes, until tender.

ec-116.title: Chicken with Green Olives (Firakh bi-l-Zatun al-Akhdar)
ec-116.culturalNotes: Recipe 116, page 53 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut each chicken into 4–6 pieces. Boil the olives in fresh water for 1 minute, drain, pit and halve them.
instructions.2: Heat the oil, stir in the mastic for 10 seconds, add the chicken, cover tightly and turn off the heat for 1–2 minutes, then fry the chicken until browned and lift it out.
instructions.3: Soften the onion in the same oil and set it aside with the chicken.
instructions.4: Fry the flour until golden. Off the heat, whisk in 1 cup of warm water a little at a time.
instructions.5: Return to the heat and, when the gravy bubbles, add the chicken, onion, salt and pepper. Cook over a very low heat for about 20 minutes.
instructions.6: Add the olives and lemon juice and simmer for 2–3 minutes more.

ec-117.title: Giblet-Stuffed Chicken, Boiled then Fried (Firakh Mahshiya wi Mihammara)
ec-117.culturalNotes: Recipe 117, page 54 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-117-i1.name: Chickens, About 1 Kg Each, With Giblets

ec-117-i2.name: Onions (2 For The Stuffing, 1 For The Broth)

instructions.1: Finely chop two onions and cut the gizzards and hearts into very small pieces. Mix them with the spice, salt and pepper.
instructions.2: Stuff the chickens with the mixture and sew them up.
instructions.3: Bring enough water to half-cover the chickens to the boil with the remaining onion and salt, add the chickens and cook for about 20 minutes, then lift them out.
instructions.4: Heat oil in another pot, stir in the mastic for 10 seconds, add the chickens, cover tightly and turn off the heat for 1–2 minutes.
instructions.5: Fry the chickens, turning them until browned all over.

ec-118.title: Giblet-Stuffed Roast Chicken (Firakh Mahshiya wi Mashwiya)
ec-118.culturalNotes: Recipe 118, page 54 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-118-i1.name: Chickens, About 1 Kg Each, With Giblets

instructions.1: Chop the onions very finely and cut the gizzards and hearts into very small pieces. Season, add the spice and mix.
instructions.2: Stuff the chickens and sew them up.
instructions.3: Mix the tomato paste, lemon juice, oil, salt and pepper and rub it all over the chickens.
instructions.4: Roast in a hot oven, basting two or three times with the juices.

ec-120.title: Lebanese Lemon Chicken with Olives (Djaj bi Leimoon Hamed)
ec-120.culturalNotes: Recipe 120, page 56 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the chickens into neat joints and fry them lightly in oil; set aside.
instructions.2: Put the onions, garlic, coriander and parsley in a pot, add the saffron and leave over a very low heat until soft.
instructions.3: Add the chicken with its oil, salt, pepper and 1 cup of hot water. Cover and cook slowly, stirring now and then.
instructions.4: When the chicken is done, move it to a platter. Mash the vegetables well, add the lemon juice and olives and let it bubble for 2–3 minutes.
instructions.5: Pour the sauce over the chicken and serve.

ec-121.title: Chicken in Pomegranate and Walnut Sauce (Fesenjan)
ec-121.culturalNotes: Recipe 121, page 56 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the chickens into neat joints, fry them lightly on all sides and keep them warm.
instructions.2: Soften the onions in the same oil.
instructions.3: Add the walnuts, broth, sugar, pomegranate juice, salt and pepper and cook until the sauce thickens.
instructions.4: Return the chicken and cook over a low heat for 20–25 minutes more.

ec-122.title: Lebanese Rice-Stuffed Chicken, Boiled then Fried (Djaj Mihshy)
ec-122.culturalNotes: Recipe 122, page 57 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-122-i1.name: Chickens, About 1 Kg Each, With Giblets

instructions.1: Dice the giblets and mix them with the rice, spice, salt and pepper. Stuff the chickens and truss or sew them closed.
instructions.2: Bring 4 cups of water to the boil with the onion and seasoning, add the chickens and cook for 20–30 minutes. Lift them out and keep warm.
instructions.3: Heat oil, stir in the mastic for a few seconds, add the chickens, cover tightly and turn off the heat for 2–3 minutes.
instructions.4: Uncover and fry the chickens until nicely browned.
instructions.5: Cut them into joints, heap the stuffing in the middle of a dish and arrange the chicken around it. Moisten the stuffing with a little warm broth if you like.

ec-123.title: Lebanese Rice-Stuffed Roast Chicken (Djaj Mihshy)
ec-123.culturalNotes: Recipe 123, page 57 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-123-i1.name: Chickens, About 1 Kg Each, With Giblets

instructions.1: Dice the giblets and mix them with the rice, spice, salt and pepper. Stuff the chickens and truss or sew them closed.
instructions.2: Thin the tomato paste with the lemon juice, add salt, pepper and the oil, and rub the mixture over the chickens inside and out.
instructions.3: Roast, basting often with the lemon mixture.

ec-124.title: Chicken Simmered in Yogurt with Mint (Firakh Matbukha bi-l-Zabadi)
ec-124.culturalNotes: Recipe 124, page 58 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the chickens into neat joints and fry them lightly in olive oil.
instructions.2: Stir the egg white into the yogurt to keep it from splitting and press it through a sieve over the chicken.
instructions.3: Season and cook uncovered for about 30 minutes.
instructions.4: Thicken with the cornflour, move to a serving dish and sprinkle with the mint.

ec-125.title: Sumac-Onion Chicken Baked in Bread (Frakh Mashwiya bi-l-Summa’)
ec-125.culturalNotes: Recipe 125, page 58 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Grate the onions and mix with the sumac, salt, pepper and olive oil.
instructions.2: Rub the chickens with the mixture and push the rest inside them.
instructions.3: Wrap each chicken in a loaf of bread, then in foil.
instructions.4: Cook slowly in the middle of a low, preheated oven until the chicken is tender.

ec-135.title: Tunisian Fish Couscous with Fish Balls (Couscous bil Hout)
ec-135.culturalNotes: Recipe 135, page 62 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-135-i4.name: Marinade: Fennel Seeds And Caraway Seeds

ec-135-i7.name: Fish Balls: Grated Onion, 3–5 Crushed Garlic Cloves, 1 Egg And Half A Stale Loaf

ec-135-i8.name: Fish Balls: Chopped Parsley, A Dash Of Harissa And Paprika

ec-135-i10.name: Onions, Zucchini, Carrots, Artichoke Hearts And Tomatoes

ec-135-i11.name: Cloves, A Piece Of Cinnamon Bark And Caraway Seeds

instructions.1: Soak the chickpeas overnight, then boil them in fresh water until tender. Drain, keeping the liquid.
instructions.2: Mix the marinade ingredients and leave the fish fillets in it for 1–2 hours.
instructions.3: Fish balls: moisten the bread with water. Steam and flake the whiting and mix it with a purée of the onion and garlic, the paprika, harissa, parsley, beaten egg, bread, salt and pepper. Roll into small balls, fry until brown and keep warm.
instructions.4: Vegetables: brown the grated onions in oil, then stir in the sliced zucchini and carrots, chopped artichokes and diced tomatoes until coated with oil. Add the spices tied in muslin, the chickpeas and enough of their liquid to cover, and cook over a low heat.
instructions.5: Sprinkle the couscous with cold water and steam it in a perforated steamer set over the vegetable pot, covered. Once or twice, uncover, sprinkle with a little cold water and fluff the grains with a fork so they do not form lumps. Keep steaming until the vegetables are tender.
instructions.6: Brush the marinade off the fish and grill the fillets on both sides.
instructions.7: Pile the couscous in a serving bowl, top with the grilled fish and fish balls, and serve the vegetables separately.

ec-136.title: Tunisian Couscous with Mutton and Dates (Couscous bi Tamr)
ec-136.culturalNotes: Recipe 136, page 64 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the meat into bite-sized cubes. Peel and dice the carrots and turnips.
instructions.2: Boil the meat and vegetables in salted water.
instructions.3: When the meat is nearly done, sprinkle the couscous with water and steam it over the pot for 5–7 minutes.
instructions.4: Uncover, sprinkle lightly with water and break up any lumps with a fork.
instructions.5: Stone and roughly chop the dates, mix them into the couscous and return it to steam over the meat until both are fully cooked. Keep them separate.
instructions.6: Pour a ladle of the meat broth over the garlic, harissa and chili and boil hard until reduced by half.
instructions.7: Serve the couscous, the meat and the sauce separately.

ec-138.title: Lebanese Chicken Maghrabiyeh
ec-138.culturalNotes: Recipe 138, page 65 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the chicken into neat joints.
instructions.2: Bring water to the boil with the onions, mastic, salt and pepper, add the chicken and cook.
instructions.3: About 10–15 minutes before the chicken is done, sprinkle the couscous with water and steam it over the broth, uncovering once or twice to break up lumps with a fork and sprinkle with more cold water.
instructions.4: When the couscous is tender, move it to a deep bowl and keep warm.
instructions.5: Lift out the chicken and fry the joints in oil.
instructions.6: Mash the onion into the broth, thicken it, check the seasoning and serve it separately as a sauce.

ec-147.title: Fried Eggplant Baked in Tahini (Bitingan Ma’li bi-l-Tahina)
ec-147.culturalNotes: Recipe 147, page 68 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Slice the eggplants lengthwise about 2 cm thick, sprinkle with salt and leave for at least an hour. Squeeze gently, drain and pat dry.
instructions.2: Deep-fry the slices until dark brown and drain on absorbent paper.
instructions.3: Make a thin tahini sauce: whisk the tahini with the water, lemon juice, vinegar, cumin, salt and garlic until smooth.
instructions.4: Arrange the eggplant in a baking pan and pour the tahini sauce over.
instructions.5: Bake in the middle of a moderate, preheated oven for 15 minutes.

ec-153.title: Mashed Fried Eggplant with Garlic Yogurt (Beitinjan Mifassakh)
ec-153.culturalNotes: Recipe 153, page 71 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Slice and salt the eggplants for an hour, then squeeze and pat dry.
instructions.2: Fry them in olive oil until soft and brown.
instructions.3: Mash with the yogurt and garlic.
instructions.4: Stir in the parsley and serve.

ec-154.title: Turkish Eggplant Cream (Hünkar Beğendi)
ec-154.culturalNotes: Recipe 154, page 71 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Roast the eggplants whole in their skins, in a hot oven or on a tray over the stove, turning them when one side softens. Peel, drain and mash the flesh.
instructions.2: Melt the butter and cook the flour in it over a very low heat until golden.
instructions.3: Off the heat, stir in the hot milk, then return to the heat and let it bubble.
instructions.4: Stir in the eggplant, season and cook for 10 minutes.
instructions.5: Off the heat, stir in the cheese and parsley and serve.

ec-155.title: Imam Bayildi with Minced Beef and Yogurt
ec-155.culturalNotes: Recipe 155, page 71 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-155-i6.name: Pine Nuts, Pecans Or Hazelnuts, Chopped

instructions.1: Slice, salt and drain the eggplants, then deep-fry them until dark brown.
instructions.2: Brown the onion in a little oil, add the beef with salt and pepper and cook until its juices are absorbed.
instructions.3: Put the meat and fried eggplant in a pot over a low heat and cook, stirring often, until the eggplant has completely broken down.
instructions.4: Press the mixture against the side of the pot with a wooden spoon to squeeze out excess fat, and pour it off.
instructions.5: Spread in a shallow dish. Mix the yogurt with the garlic and a little salt and spread it over the top.
instructions.6: Sprinkle with the nuts and serve hot or cold.

ec-158.title: Imam Bayildi: Baked Eggplant Shells with Currants
ec-158.culturalNotes: Recipe 158, page 73 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Soak the currants in lukewarm water.
instructions.2: Halve the eggplants lengthwise and scoop out the flesh without piercing the skins. Dice or mash the flesh and sprinkle it with lemon juice.
instructions.3: Fry the eggplant flesh with the onions in the oil, then add the tomatoes, parsley, thyme, bay leaf, salt and pepper. Cover and cook over a low heat for about 20 minutes.
instructions.4: Off the heat, stir in the garlic and the drained currants.
instructions.5: Arrange the eggplant shells in a well-greased baking dish and fill them with the mixture.
instructions.6: Drizzle a little olive oil over each and bake in a slow oven until the shells are soft.

ec-161.title: Poached Fish Sayadiya with Brown Onion Rice (Sayadiyit al-Samak)
ec-161.culturalNotes: Recipe 161, page 74 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Fry the onion in the oil until deep brown.
instructions.2: Add about 2 cups of water with salt and pepper and bring to the boil.
instructions.3: Add the fish and poach over a low heat for 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Strain the broth, top it up with water and use it to cook the rice (fry the rice briefly in a little oil first, then simmer until the liquid is absorbed).
instructions.5: Skin, bone and flake the fish and fold it through the rice.

ec-164.title: Fried Fish Sayadiya (Sayadiyit Samak Ma’li)
ec-164.culturalNotes: Recipe 164, page 75 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the fish into neat pieces, fry them and drain on absorbent paper.
instructions.2: Fry the onion in the same oil until deep brown.
instructions.3: Add the rice and water with salt and cook uncovered until the water has been absorbed.
instructions.4: Lay the fried fish on top of the rice, turn the heat to its lowest, cover and cook for 15–20 minutes.
instructions.5: Serve the fish on its rice.

ec-167.title: Fish and Vegetables Baked in Tahini (Samak bi-l-Khudar wi-l-Tahina)
ec-167.culturalNotes: Recipe 167, page 76 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-167-i5.name: Sweet Peppers, Seeded And Thinly Sliced

ec-167-i7.name: Tahini Sauce (tahini Thinned With Water, Lemon, Vinegar, Cumin And Salt)

instructions.1: Cut the fish into large chunks, coat them in seasoned flour and fry. Drain, cool and flake.
instructions.2: Parboil the carrots and slice them thinly.
instructions.3: Sauté the onions and sweet peppers and mix them into the fish with the carrots and eggs.
instructions.4: Spread the mixture in a baking pan and cover it with the tahini sauce.
instructions.5: Bake in the middle of a moderate, preheated oven for 15 minutes.

ec-177.title: Gulf-Style Baked Fish with Tomato and Tamarind (Samak bi Salsat al-Tamata wal-Sabbar)
ec-177.culturalNotes: Recipe 177, page 81 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-177-i3.name: Tamarind (soaked And Strained To 1/2 Cup Concentrate)

instructions.1: Split the fish lengthwise from head to tail and open it out like a book.
instructions.2: Dissolve the tomato paste in the tamarind liquid and set aside.
instructions.3: Blend the garlic, lemon juice, mixed spice and half the fresh coriander. Rub half of this mixture over the fish and leave it to rest.
instructions.4: Lay the fish on an oiled baking tray and bake until cooked through.
instructions.5: Meanwhile, fry the onions and peppers in olive oil until soft, then stir in the ground coriander, cumin, ginger and salt.
instructions.6: Spread the onion mixture and the diced tomatoes over the baked fish, scatter over the remaining coriander and pour the tamarind sauce on top.
instructions.7: Return to the oven for 5–7 minutes so the fish takes on the flavours, then serve.

ec-178.title: Tunisian Breaded Fish in Spicy Tomato Sauce (Hout Moqly)
ec-178.culturalNotes: Recipe 178, page 81 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Marinate the fish in the lemon juice and salt.
instructions.2: Fry the onions and zucchini lightly in olive oil, then add the garlic, harissa, salt, pepper and the tomato paste thinned with 1 cup of water. Cook for 15 minutes.
instructions.3: Mash the sauce and boil it again until reduced and thick.
instructions.4: Dip the fish in beaten egg, coat with breadcrumbs and deep-fry.
instructions.5: Arrange on a serving dish and spoon the tomato sauce over.

ec-179.title: Tunisian Grilled Fish with Eggplant Sauce (Sharmoulit Badinjan)
ec-179.culturalNotes: Recipe 179, page 82 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Slice, salt and drain the eggplants, then fry them in olive oil until dark brown.
instructions.2: Grill the fish and keep it warm.
instructions.3: Brown the onions in the eggplant oil, add the garlic, harissa, tabil and the tomato paste thinned with 1 cup of water, and cook over a medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring often.
instructions.4: Mash the eggplant with the vinegar and some salt and stir it into the tomato sauce. Cook for 3–5 minutes more.
instructions.5: Pour the sauce over the grilled fish and serve.

ec-180.title: Jordanian Sayadiyeh (Fish in Dark Onion Broth with Rice)
ec-180.culturalNotes: Recipe 180, page 82 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Marinate the fish in the lemon juice and salt for 1–2 hours.
instructions.2: Fry the onions until very brown, then add the garlic and fry, stirring constantly so it does not stick.
instructions.3: Take the pan off the heat and mash the onions well with the back of a spoon. Add the spices, seasoning and plenty of water.
instructions.4: Bring back to the boil, add the fish and cook until tender. The broth should be very dark.
instructions.5: Keep back just enough broth to cover the fish. Fry the rice in oil until every grain is coated, add broth to make 1 1/2 times the volume of the rice, season and cook until tender.
instructions.6: Serve the rice and the fish in its broth separately.

ec-181.title: Iraqi Baked Fish Stuffed with Walnuts and Pomegranate (Samaka Harra)
ec-181.culturalNotes: Recipe 181, page 83 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Soak the bulgur for an hour.
instructions.2: Pound or blend the bulgur with the garlic, onions, walnuts, parsley, coriander, lemon juice and salt until well mixed.
instructions.3: Stir in the pomegranate seeds and stuff the fish with the mixture.
instructions.4: Put the fish and any extra stuffing in a well-oiled baking dish and cover with foil.
instructions.5: Bake in a hot, preheated oven for 30 minutes, then lower to moderate and bake for 30 minutes more.

ec-183.title: Spiced Boiled Gizzards with Mastic (‘Awanis Maslu’a)
ec-183.culturalNotes: Recipe 183, page 84 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Tie the mastic and cardamom in a muslin bag.
instructions.2: Boil 4–5 cups of water with the spice bag, the onion and salt.
instructions.3: Add the gizzards and cook for 10–12 minutes.
instructions.4: Use the gizzards in the dishes that follow, and the broth to cook rice or vermicelli.

ec-184.title: Gizzards and Pearl Onions Baked in Béchamel (‘Awanis bi-l-Bechamel)
ec-184.culturalNotes: Recipe 184, page 84 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Boil the gizzards with mastic, cardamom and onion as in the spiced boiled gizzards recipe.
instructions.2: Peel the pearl onions, leaving them whole, parboil in salted water and drain.
instructions.3: Halve the gizzards and put them in a deep baking dish with the onions.
instructions.4: Stir the nutmeg into the béchamel and pour it over.
instructions.5: Bake in a moderate, preheated oven for 20 minutes, until the top is browned.

ec-185.title: Gizzard and Vegetable Casserole (Tagin ‘Awanis)
ec-185.culturalNotes: Recipe 185, page 84 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Parboil the carrots, potatoes and peas in salted water and drain. Slice the carrots thinly and dice the potatoes.
instructions.2: Put the vegetables and gizzards in a casserole.
instructions.3: Stir the cornflour and mixed spices into the well-seasoned gizzard broth and pour it over.
instructions.4: Bake in a moderate, preheated oven for 30–40 minutes.

ec-186.title: Gizzards in Tomato Sauce (‘Awanis bi-l-Dim‘a)
ec-186.culturalNotes: Recipe 186, page 85 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Tomato sauce: soften the onions in oil, add the garlic and fry until pale brown, then add the tomato juice and simmer for 15–20 minutes until dark. Add the vinegar, salt and pepper and cook for 2–3 minutes.
instructions.2: Halve the gizzards and parboil them for 3–5 minutes, then drain.
instructions.3: Add them to the tomato sauce with the mixed spice.
instructions.4: Simmer over a very low heat for 20–30 minutes.

ec-189.title: Freekeh with Gizzards (Firik Matbukh bi-l-‘Awanis)
ec-189.culturalNotes: Recipe 189, page 86 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Clean the freekeh: rub it in a bowl of water so the chaff floats and grit sinks, and rinse until the water runs clear.
instructions.2: Bring the gizzard broth to the boil, topped up with water to make 5 cups.
instructions.3: Add the freekeh and cook for 15 minutes.
instructions.4: Halve the gizzards and mix them into the freekeh.
instructions.5: Pour the melted butter over and cook over a very low heat for 10–15 minutes more, until the freekeh is soft.

ec-191.title: Fried Beef Head Meat (Lahmit al-Ras Ma’liya)
ec-191.culturalNotes: Recipe 191, page 87 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Blanch the meat and drain it (head meat is always sold boned).
instructions.2: Return it to the pot with the chopped onion, peppercorns, salt and just enough water to cover, and cook until tender.
instructions.3: Drain the meat and fry it in the oil.
instructions.4: Strain the stock, thicken it with the cornflour and serve it in a separate bowl.

ec-192.title: Braised Beef Head Meat (Lahmit al-Ras Matbukha)
ec-192.culturalNotes: Recipe 192, page 87 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Rub the onion with salt, pepper and mixed spice.
instructions.2: Put it in a pot with the meat and oil and cook over a very low heat until the meat has reabsorbed the juices it releases.
instructions.3: Add a little water, and more whenever it dries out, and cook until the meat is tender, about 45 minutes.

ec-194.title: Jellied Sheep’s Head Terrine (Jilatin al-Ras)
ec-194.culturalNotes: Recipe 194, page 88 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-194-i9.name: Egg (whole, With Its Crushed Shell, To Clear The Stock)

instructions.1: Have the skull split lengthwise. Soak it in several changes of salted water, singe off any hairs and scrape it with a blunt knife, then wash under running water and blanch.
